item.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor
item.brief: Update listItems(transport) in this repository so it resolves to every item in order by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. Add or update tests with a fake transport covering a single page, multiple pages, a missing next_cursor field, and order preservation. Update the README to document that listItems follows pagination. Keep npm test passing. Commit the change on the working branch; do not push.

pr.body: listItems(transport) requests /items with no cursor, then passes each page's next_cursor back unchanged as `cursor` until it is null or absent. It throws on a page without an items array or a page that repeats its cursor. Files: client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md. Checks: npm test 9/9 pass (baseline 3/3). Assumption: items are returned in server page order, which the API sorts by id. Follow-ups (non-blocking): cycle detection covers only a self-loop; README 'ordered by id' wording could read 'in server order'.
pr.summary: listItems follows pagination. now returns every item in order. before: first page only, now: all pages until next_cursor is null or absent, cursor passed back unchanged.
pr.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor across pages

agt_01M88RVE08XSFGRP9G4N80R4Z1:1.description: The repeated-cursor guard in client.js only catches a page whose next_cursor equals the cursor just sent. A longer cycle (A -> B -> A) would loop forever. The spec does not require cycle detection, and the test name is accurate for the self-loop case it covers. Optional follow-up: track a Set of seen cursors.

agt_01M88RVE08XSFGRP9G4N80R4Z1:2.description: README still says listItems returns items 'ordered by id'. That wording predates this commit, and the code preserves server page order without sorting. Consider rewording to 'in server order' unless the server guarantees id order.

agt_01M88RVE08XSFGRP9G4N80R4Z1:3.description: The pagedTransport helper keys pages by cursor, so an unexpected cursor returns a 400 and fails the test. That is the intended behaviour. No change needed; noted only for test-design awareness.

risk.why: Contained behaviour change to one public client function (now multiple requests). No security, concurrency or persistence impact. Tests cover single page, multi-page, missing next_cursor, order and failure paths. Reviewer rated it low; medium chosen because the call pattern changes.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: Implement cursor pagination for GET /items in this repository per the shared contract. Accept optional limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string from a previous response). Return {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}, ordered by id, next_cursor null on the last page. Invalid limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error": "..."}. Add unit tests covering default and max limit, invalid values, multi-page traversal with no gaps or duplicates, and the last page. Update the README to document the parameters and response shape. Keep python3 -m unittest passing. Commit the change on the working branch; do not push.

state.summary:
Added cursor pagination to GET /items in inventory-api, committed on archon/hqqjx6r0-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items as f824b14 (not pushed). `limit` (integer 1..100, default 20) and `cursor` (the id of the last item on the previous page) are optional. The response is {"items", "next_cursor"}, ordered by id, with next_cursor null on the last page. A bad limit or cursor returns 400 with {"error"}. Tests cover default and max limit, invalid values, multi-page traversal (limit 10, ids 1..57, no gaps or duplicates), the last page, and an exact-fit page. README documents the parameters and response shape. Checks: `python3 -m unittest` passes 11/11 on f824b14. Before the change, the new tests fail against the original api.py (16 failures, 3 errors across subtests). An independent reviewer (agt_01M88RVNJCZ2K5QW9SP0K8WM4E) passed the change at f824b14 with no findings, risk low. Non-blocking follow-up: a non-string query value (e.g. a JSON integer passed via api_cli.py) raises AttributeError instead of returning 400. This also applies to the existing handler, and the request contract is {str: str}. Nothing is left running. The client side (inventory-client listItems) is out of scope for this stage.

pr.body: Approach: keyset pagination on id. cursor is the last id of the previous page; the next page is items with id greater than cursor, sorted by id. Key files: api.py (list_items, _parse_limit, _parse_cursor), test_api.py (new pagination tests), README.md (endpoint docs). Checks: python3 -m unittest 11/11 OK at f824b14. New tests fail on the original api.py, confirming they cover the change. Reviewer passed f824b14 with no findings. Assumptions: cursor is the plain decimal id, documented as opaque; a deleted id still works as a cursor because the filter is id > cursor. Limits: non-string query values raise AttributeError (pre-existing pattern, non-blocking follow-up).
pr.summary: Made GET /items paginate. Now can request limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor; response is {items, next_cursor}. Before: all items, no paging. Now: 20 per page by default, null next_cursor on last page, 400 on bad limit or cursor.
pr.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
